description: Ubuntu apt package profile for the personal-dotfiles bootstrap. Every package is installed with --no-install-recommends. Tools that apt ships too old (fzf, neovim, nodejs) come from manifests/tools.json instead and must not be installed from apt.

keys.targets: Supported Ubuntu release -> codename. Architectures are the dpkg names; installer/platform.py maps x86_64/aarch64 onto them.
keys.apt_policy: How every apt install in this profile is invoked. install_recommends=false is mandatory, see reason.
keys.forbidden: Regular expressions matched against the full simulated package list (apt-get -s). Any match is a hard failure before installing anything.
keys.groups: Ordered package groups. default=true groups are part of the one-line install. Each package names why the reviewed configuration needs it.
keys.repositories: Third-party apt sources the installer writes. Keys are verified by primary fingerprint, never by file hash, because vendors add subkeys over time.
keys.shims: Command names the configuration calls that Ubuntu ships under a different name. The installer creates these links in the tools.json bin_dir.
keys.system_steps: Root-owned configuration beyond package installation, each guarded by a check so reruns are no-ops.
keys.not_from_apt: Packages that exist in the Ubuntu archive but must not be installed from it, and why.
keys.release_notes: Per-release differences that change behaviour, including known degraded features.
keys.evidence: Where and how this profile was last checked.

apt_policy.reason: With Recommends enabled, python3-pip pulls build-essential, gcc/g++, make and python3-dev on both releases and both architectures, and google-chrome-stable's Ubuntu dependencies pull cpp. gnome-terminal Recommends (gvfs, yelp, nautilus-extension-gnome-terminal) are not needed for the configured behaviour. Without Recommends no forbidden package appears in any of the four cells.

forbidden.reason: Desktop environments, display managers, container stacks, ROS, forge CLIs, a C/C++ toolchain, apt Node.js and the apt fzf/neovim builds are out of scope. nvm, conda and pyenv are not apt packages and are never installed by this profile.

packages.name: zsh
packages.reason: Login and interactive shell (zsh/zshrc, zsh/zshenv).

packages.name: tmux
packages.reason: tmux/tmux.conf, bin/tmux-attach, bin/tmux-smart-paste. 22.04 ships 3.2a, see release_notes.

packages.name: git
packages.reason: Repository clone/update, antidote plugin clones, TPM, fzf-git.sh widgets.

packages.name: curl
packages.reason: Bootstrap and verified artifact downloads for manifests/tools.json.

packages.name: ca-certificates
packages.reason: TLS for git and curl on minimal images.

packages.name: xz-utils
packages.reason: Node.js and OMX native assets are .tar.xz archives.

packages.name: gpgv
packages.reason: Detached-signature checks for Node.js SHASUMS256.txt and the Claude Code manifest. Already a dependency of apt; listed so the requirement is explicit.

packages.name: locales
packages.reason: zsh/zshenv exports LANG/LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 when unset; see system_steps.

packages.name: wl-clipboard
packages.reason: Wayland backend for bin/pbcopy, bin/pbpaste and bin/tmux-smart-paste (wl-copy, wl-paste).

packages.name: xclip
packages.reason: X11 backend for bin/pbcopy, bin/pbpaste and bin/tmux-smart-paste.

packages.name: python3
packages.reason: Installer runtime and user Python.

packages.name: python3-pip
packages.reason: Requested pip, used inside virtual environments only. Never with --user or --break-system-packages.

packages.name: python3-venv
packages.reason: Requested venv.

packages.name: ripgrep
packages.reason: zsh/zsh.d/envs.zsh FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND, bin/rg.fzf, neovim fzf-lua grep.

packages.name: fd-find
packages.reason: tmux prefix-@ file picker calls fd (installed as fdfind, see shims).

packages.name: tree
packages.reason: fzf Alt-C preview in zsh/zsh.d/envs.zsh.

groups.note: Installed even without a running desktop; settings are applied later by the GUI phase. None of these pull GNOME Shell, a session or a display manager.

packages.name: libglib2.0-bin
packages.reason: gsettings and gdbus, used by installer/gui.py to apply GNOME settings and probe the user D-Bus session.

packages.name: dconf-cli
packages.reason: installer/gui.py reads dconf to tell explicit GNOME settings from defaults before overwriting them, so restore can reset unset keys instead of pinning defaults.

packages.name: gnome-terminal
packages.reason: Default terminal whose tab/window shortcuts are managed.

packages.name: input-remapper
packages.reason: Ctrl+Super+Left/Right -> Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown intent. 22.04 ships 1.4.0, 24.04 ships 2.0.1; adapters are version specific. input-remapper-daemon ships a system service, udev rule, D-Bus policy and an XDG autostart entry.

packages.name: google-chrome-stable
packages.reason: Browser whose tab navigation is part of the managed shortcuts.

google-chrome.reason_for_paths: google-chrome-stable's postinst rewrites exactly this .sources file and keyring and removes a legacy google-chrome.list. Writing the same paths and values first means the package takes them over instead of leaving a duplicate source with a conflicting Signed-By.
google-chrome.version_pinning: Not possible: the repository only publishes the current build. The installer records the installed version; it does not pin one.

observed.depends: ca-certificates, fonts-liberation, libasound2, libatk-bridge2.0-0, libatk1.0-0, libatspi2.0-0, libc6 (>= 2.25), libcairo2, libcups2, libcurl3-gnutls | libcurl3-nss | libcurl4 | libcurl3, libdbus-1-3, libexpat1, libgbm1, libglib2.0-0, libgtk-3-0 | libgtk-4-1, libnspr4, libnss3, libpango-1.0-0, libudev1, libvulkan1, libx11-6, libxcb1, libxcomposite1, libxdamage1, libxext6, libxfixes3, libxkbcommon0, libxrandr2, wget, xdg-utils
observed.side_effects: Installs /etc/cron.daily/google-chrome, which re-checks the repository configuration daily.

shims.name: fd
shims.reason: Ubuntu's fd-find installs fdfind; tmux/tmux.conf calls fd.

system_steps.reason: zsh/zshenv falls back to en_US.UTF-8; minimal images ship only C.UTF-8.

not_from_apt.fzf: jammy 0.29, noble 0.44. The configuration needs >= 0.66 (fzf --raw in zsh/zsh.d/alias.zsh), --accept-nth (0.60+) in bin/tmux-attach and --tmux (0.53+). Use tools.json.
not_from_apt.neovim: jammy 0.6.1, noble 0.9.5. nvim/init.lua refuses to load plugins below 0.11 and warns below 0.12. Use tools.json.
not_from_apt.nodejs: jammy 12, noble 18. OMX requires node >= 20. Use tools.json; do not replace an unrelated system Node.
not_from_apt.bat: Optional preview in zsh/zsh.d/envs.zsh; the configuration checks for it and works without it. Not selected.
not_from_apt.eza: Optional ls replacement; guarded by command -v. Not selected.

unavoidable_runtime_dependencies.libx11-6 and other X11 client libraries,: xclip, GTK and Chrome. Client libraries only; no X server.
unavoidable_runtime_dependencies.mesa-libgallium, libllvm20 (24.04 only): libgbm1 for google-chrome-stable. A GPU driver runtime library, not a compiler toolchain.

tmux.decision: Accept the Ubuntu package. tmux publishes no official prebuilt binaries, the 24.04 package needs glibc 2.38, and building from source would add a C toolchain.
tmux.config_load: tmux/tmux.conf loads with no errors on 3.2a (parse-only and execute).
degraded: allow-passthrough does not exist before 3.3; set -gq silently ignores it, so terminal passthrough sequences are dropped.
Window drag-to-reorder on the status line (the %if >= 3.4 block) is not bound.
fzf --tmux popups fail on 3.2a (display-popup rejects fzf's border options): prefix-S session picker (bin/tmux-attach) and prefix-@ file picker. Needs a tmux < 3.3 fallback in the configuration.

24.04.python3: 3.12; pip outside a venv is blocked by PEP 668, which matches the venv-only policy.

evidence.method: Rootless apt simulation (private Dir, empty dpkg status) against Ubuntu main+universe with -updates and -security for jammy/noble x amd64/arm64, plus a private copy of each root with the Google Chrome repository added. No containers or VMs.
evidence.forbidden_with_recommends: build-essential, gcc, g++, cpp, make, binutils, libc6-dev, python3-dev (all four cells)
evidence.not_proven: Actual installation, package postinst behaviour, GUI behaviour and arm64 execution were not tested by simulation.
